knowledge.statement: The inflated accepted index follows from the resume point being compared against the index the StopSign occupies in the receiving replica's accounting: sync_log computes accepted_idx = LogSync.sync_idx + LogSync.suffix.len() and adds one for a carried StopSign, while the StopSign occupies the index accepted_idx - 1 and the sender attaches it without shifting sync_idx. The condition is therefore sync_idx + suffix.len() >= the StopSign's index, and it does not depend on the snapshot option: the no-snapshot branch passes the caller's common_prefix_idx unchanged (a re-promising follower's accepted index, or a candidate leader's decided index), whereas the snapshot branch passes the compacted index returned by create_diff_snapshot, which is derived from get_decided_idx_without_stopsign and therefore excludes the StopSign.
knowledge.conditions: Holds for any LogSync whose stopsign is Some; the snapshot branch is only entered when T::Snapshot::use_snapshots() is true and the sender's decided index exceeds common_prefix_idx. Observed producer instances: a follower re-synchronized after reconnected() at the same ballot (8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8, 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63), a follower re-presenting its accepted index when it re-promises in a new term after an ordinary leader change (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 11), and a candidate leader that syncs from such a follower (dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea event 13). No snapshot-enabled execution has been run; the successor submitted here exercises that option.

knowledge.conditions: Leader candidate in the prepare phase that receives a promise with a higher accepted round; the follower's Promise carries create_log_sync(prep.decided_idx, prep.decided_idx) and its stored StopSign. interpretations.rationale: Four receipts now support one index-space confusion and three of its consequences. (1) A replica that already accepted the configuration's StopSign and receives a resume point that covers it ends one index past its content: observed for a follower re-synchronized after reconnected() (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 35), for a follower that merely re-promised in a new term after an ordinary leader change with no reconnected() call (6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 11), and now for the leader itself once it takes over from a follower whose Promise carries the StopSign (dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea event 13: accepted 7 over six indices, read(5) None, decided-log read one element). In each case the replica's own reconfiguration endpoint flips from true to false and its decided log stops being readable at its real content. (2) When a write quorum of inflated reports reaches a leader, that leader decides the reported index although it holds fewer indices (8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8 and 9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 24), which then hides the reconfiguration from that leader as well. The newterm stage shows the same progression: the follower that re-promised was inflated (event 11) while the new leader and the cut-off node stayed at 6/6 (events 9, 10), and in the following stage the node that took over was itself inflated (event 13) together with both other nodes at accepted 7 and a one-element decided read (events 12, 14), i.e. the corruption propagates across authority changes. Controls in every run held: the pre-change samples (events 6-8) and the no-reconnect control (events 9-11 of the first receipt) kept accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true and a six-element decided log for every replica. The remaining scope question is the snapshot option, which the submitted successor exercises with an Entry whose Snapshot::use_snapshots() is true, since the source says the same branch is taken whenever the resume point equals the sender's decided index.

The leader-side inflation witness is entangled with the propagation stage: when the cut-off node took over, all three nodes ended at accepted 7 with decided 7 and a one-element decided read (dda5bb4179154e3abe90e69f5267b3ea events 12-14), so that stage shows the leader's own accepted index exceeded its six indices of content but does not by itself separate its recomputation from the followers' later reports; the isolated single-replica cases (event 35 of the second receipt, event 11 of the third) are the clean witnesses of the resume-point effect.

The leader-side phantom decision requires a write quorum of inflated reporters in one term (two of three nodes); a single inflated follower, or one inflated follower plus a node that received nothing, left the leader consistent (9125b6a531234e7d9d2fa8cbb817df63 event 37; 6cdcff36336646859bffb9e8c3e39789 event 9).

The documented reconfiguration flow (agent-source/docs/omnipaxos/reconfiguration.md 25-34) expects a new instance once a node observes LogEntry::StopSign(ss, true), which narrows the window in which a user reads the old instance, but the leader never observes the decision after the corruption and the followers keep reporting it while their decided log silently loses the entries.
limitations: No snapshot-enabled execution had been run when this account was written; the submitted successor runs the same resync scenario with an Entry whose Snapshot::use_snapshots() is true, and the source says that in this scenario the snapshot branch is not entered and that branch would derive sync_idx without the StopSign when it is entered.

Loss-triggered and timer-triggered re-synchronization were not exercised: messages were delivered in FIFO order without loss and no tick() timers ran, so the observed producers are explicit reconnected() calls and ordinary leader changes with one node cut off.

The consequence is bounded by the sealed configuration: after the StopSign is accepted no further entries can be accepted, so the phantom decided index carries no value and no value can be mis-assigned; the demonstrated effects are the corrupted index accounting, the unreadable or blank decided log and the lost reconfiguration endpoint rather than divergent values.

All three nodes used in-memory storage; persistence across a restart and other storages' behaviour on out-of-range reads (a storage-implementer responsibility per the Storage trait) were not exercised.
Only three-node clusters were exercised; larger clusters and repeated leader changes beyond the one newterm/staleleader sequence were not.

interpretations.rationale: Source reading of the re-synchronization path (PrepareReq -> Prepare -> Promise -> AcceptSync -> Accepted) suggests that a replica which has accepted the StopSign gets its accepted index inflated by one when it is re-synchronized at the same ballot: in handle_promise_accept the leader calls send_accsync, whose first branch uses the follower's own accepted index as the valid prefix (leader.rs 150-191), and that index already includes the StopSign because set_stopsign adds it (internal_storage.rs 503-512). create_log_sync then reports that index as LogSync.sync_idx with the sender's StopSign attached, and sync_log adds the StopSign once more, so the follower's accepted index ends at prefix + suffix + 1 while its decided index is the AcceptSync's decided index (internal_storage.rs 313-360). The follower then reports that inflated index in Accepted (follower.rs 112-126), and the leader's decision rule accepts any incoming accepted index whose count reaches a write quorum (leader.rs 316-345), so a write quorum of inflated reports would set the leader's decided index past the entries it holds. Both endpoints this reading endangers are public: is_reconfigured() is gated on stopsign_is_decided() (mod.rs 284-290, state_cache.rs 123-126), the bool of LogEntry::StopSign is documented as 'the reconfiguration has been decided' (util.rs 277-279), and the documented user flow reads the decided suffix and switches configuration only on StopSign(.., true) (reconfiguration.md 25-34). The final judgment is left unresolved until the two-case execution samples the endpoints; the reading also predicts that a fresh or lagging follower, whose prefix does not yet contain the StopSign, is unaffected. Counterevidence and limits: the reconfiguration documentation tells the user to start a new instance once the StopSign is observed as decided, so the affected window is an old instance that keeps running after (or while) it observes the decision and then re-synchronizes; the accounting is correct whenever sync_idx stays at or below the StopSign's own index, which covers the normal catch-up path; the account rests on static reading of the read() combination paths and of MemoryStorage's empty-range behaviour, not on an executed observation.

Confirmed by execution: the re-synchronization of a replica that already accepted its configuration's StopSign inflates its reported accepted index by one, and a write quorum of such reports makes the leader decide an index past every entry it holds. Receipt 8b314551f1e049fcbf73a358f8ddf2c8, two cases in one run over three real OmniPaxos instances with MemoryStorage (events: 19,20,21 = after the StopSign was decided on all three nodes; 22,23 = the two re-synchronized followers; 24 = the leader; 9,10,11 = the identical prefix without reconnected()). Before the re-synchronization all three nodes reported accepted 6, decided 6, is_reconfigured true, read(5) = StopSign with decided = true, and read_decided_suffix(0) = six elements.
